title: Ask the Critical Question
coreMove: Interrogate each external cue by asking whether it serves the thing you meant to do right now.
sourcePressure: The chapter opens the external-trigger section with a fast filter: does this cue serve prior intent or pull the reader away from it.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would treat all alerts as bad instead of judging each cue against prior intent and real obligations.

hook: Ask the Critical Question as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: air-quality inspector receiving a sensor alert during report writing
exampleSpecs.audience: inspector deciding whether an alert deserves immediate action
exampleSpecs.stakes: a real hazard must not be ignored, but routine noise must not own the day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she checks whether the alert protects today's inspection intent or belongs in the afternoon review batch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A particulate sensor alert flashes beside an inspection report draft.

exampleSpecs.domain: violin repair apprentice hearing the shop bell during varnish work
exampleSpecs.audience: apprentice with delicate wet varnish on the bench
exampleSpecs.stakes: one interruption can ruin a finish or serve a waiting customer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he asks whether the bell serves the varnish block or whether the front-desk sign already covers it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A wet varnish brush rests over a violin rib form.

exampleSpecs.domain: social worker receiving a group text during case notes
exampleSpecs.audience: caseworker sorting urgency from social pull
exampleSpecs.stakes: documentation quality and client safety both matter
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she reads the first line only, names it as logistics not crisis, and returns to the case note
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A case note draft sits under a purple agency lanyard.

exampleSpecs.domain: bird-survey volunteer hearing a rare-sighting ping
exampleSpecs.audience: volunteer who scheduled a transect count
exampleSpecs.stakes: data integrity suffers if novelty beats the planned count
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he asks if chasing the sighting serves the transect goal, then logs the current count first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A transect tally card is tucked beneath binocular straps.

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant bookkeeper receiving supplier sale emails
exampleSpecs.stakes: cheap inventory distracts from wage accuracy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, she opens every sale; after, she routes purchase cues to the buying block
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A payroll register sits next to a seafood price bulletin.

exampleSpecs.domain: court-reporter trainee seeing a software-update prompt
exampleSpecs.stakes: the update may matter later but destroys the timed drill now
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks the question, defers the prompt, and restarts the transcript timer
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A stenotype paper strip curls beside an update prompt.

choose the action that stays inside Ask the Critical Question's source pressure rather than adjacent productivity advice
explain why the tempting weak version fails: A weak run would treat all alerts as bad instead of judging each cue against prior intent and real obligations.

tryThisNowSpec: When the next cue arrives, ask whether it moves the scheduled block forward; answer yes, no, or real obligation before acting.
